Definition: Species name; printed name kept, except the typo "Hypsignathus mostrosus" corrected to "Hypsignathus monstrosus" as in TABLE1 and TABLE2
Note: The snapshot keeps the name as printed

Definition: Traditional grouping printed in the table: Microbat or Megabat
Mass of the cerebral cortex as a percentage of the mass of the brain
Note: Printed with one decimal. Cerebral cortex includes the hippocampus and the underlying white matter (Methods 2.2); brain mass excludes the olfactory bulbs (Methods 2.3). The structure masses themselves are not printed anywhere in the paper
Source Note: Caption: "shown as percentages of total mass or number of neurons in the brain"

Definition: Number of neurons in the cerebral cortex as a percentage of the number of neurons in the brain
Note: Printed with one decimal. Equals 100 x NCX (TABLE2) / NBRAIN (TABLE1) within rounding for all 13 species (internal_checks/)

Definition: Mass of the cerebellum as a percentage of the mass of the brain
Note: Printed with one decimal. See MCX/MBR

Definition: Number of neurons in the cerebellum as a percentage of the number of neurons in the brain
Note: Printed with one decimal. Equals 100 x NCB (TABLE2) / NBRAIN (TABLE1) within rounding for all 13 species (internal_checks/)

Definition: Mass of the cerebral cortex divided by the mass of the cerebellum
Note: Printed with two decimals. Equals MCX/MBR divided by MCB/MBR within rounding (table check in the item script)

Definition: Number of neurons in the cerebellum divided by the number of neurons in the cerebral cortex
Note: Printed with two decimals. Equals NCB/NBR divided by NCX/NBR within rounding (table check in the item script) and NCB / NCX of TABLE2 (internal_checks/)

Definition: One row per species; species values are means of the animals studied (n = 2 per species; TABLE1, column n)

Isotropic fractionator. For every species except Chaerephon pumilus one hemisphere was available and the paper's data are twice the numbers obtained for it (Methods 2.1; TABLE1 marks each species (1H each) or (2H each)). Percentages and ratios do not depend on that doubling
Note: No unit conversion: percentages and ratios are kept as printed
